mainTopic: Salt water and salting on שבת, and healing the eyes on שבת
overview: The משנה forbids making brine (הילמי) on שבת but allows ordinary salt water for dipping bread. רבי יוסי objects that a little or a lot is still brine, and he allows only salt water made with oil first. The גמרא explains the first view as large versus small amounts. It concludes, with רבה, רבי יוחנן and a supporting ברייתא, that רבי יוסי forbids both amounts. A set of teachings from רבי יהודה בר חביבא follows. Strong salt water, which an egg floats in, is forbidden. Salting radishes is forbidden, though dipping them while eating is fine. An אתרוג, a radish and an egg are hard to digest. רב דימי reports that no one drowns in the Sea of Sodom, which leads to rulings on healing on שבת: washing in its water is allowed, and wine or eye salve may go on the eye but not inside it. The amud ends with health advice about eye care and a list of body parts a hand should not touch, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה permits ordinary salt water
steps.stepSummary: The משנה (continuing from the ban on brine) says a person may make salt water to dip bread in or to add to cooked food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a person may make salt water, dip his bread in it, and put it into a cooked dish.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of a משנה that started on the previous page by forbidding brine (הילמי) on שבת. Here it says ordinary salt water for eating is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל ('but') contrasts this with the earlier ban on הילמי, which is strong brine used for pickling. Salt water made for immediate eating is permitted. The משנה does not yet say what exactly separates the two, and the גמרא will ask about this.

keyTerms.meaning: Brine: strong salt water used for pickling (forbidden in the first half of the משנה)

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה הוּא אֶת מֵי הַמֶּלַח,
phrases.english: But he may make salt water,
phrases.notes: 'But' contrasts with the ban on brine at the end of the previous page.

phrases.english: and dip his bread in it,
and put it into the cooked dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה הוּא אֶת מֵי הַמֶּלַח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ordinary salt water for dipping bread or adding to food may be made on שבת (in contrast to brine).

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a little or a lot, it is still brine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי objects that there is no real difference between large and small amounts, since both are brine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: But isn't it brine, whether there is a lot or a little?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues with the first view in the משנה. He says the amount does not change what the liquid is: it is brine either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words assume the first view separated brine from salt water by amount, and the גמרא will confirm that reading. What רבי יוסי concludes from his point (forbid both, or permit both) is left unclear, and the גמרא will debate it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
But isn't it brine,
whether it is a lot or a little!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא הוּא הֵילְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the distinction the first view drew between brine and salt water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Large and small amounts of salt water are the same kind of thing: brine.

steps.title: The permitted way: put oil in first
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the salt water that is permitted: one first puts oil into the water or into the salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the salt water that is permitted: one first puts oil into the water or into the salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by describing a permitted way of making salt water: add oil at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding oil first means the mixture is not made the normal brine way, so it does not look like making brine. This line becomes important later: רבה uses it to show what רבי יוסי really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: At the start, from the outset

steps.whyThisMatters: In step 8, רבה argues that a permitted method only makes sense if רבי יוסי forbids ordinary salt water.

phrases.english: And this is the salt water that is permitted:
one puts oil in at the start
into the water or into the salt.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salt water is permitted when oil is put into the water or the salt from the start.

steps.title: What is the משנה saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the first view of the משנה means when it forbids brine but permits salt water.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for an explanation of the משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brine and salt water are both salt dissolved in water, so it is unclear what difference the משנה has in mind. The גמרא wants the exact line that separates forbidden from permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
What is he saying? (asking for the meaning)

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is he saying?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What difference between brine and salt water does the משנה intend?

steps.title: שמואל: a large amount is forbidden, a small amount is allowed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the difference is quantity: a large amount of salt water is forbidden and a small amount is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This is what he means: one may not make a large amount of salt water, but one may make a small amount.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. The difference between brine and permitted salt water is only how much is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large batch looks like it is being prepared for pickling, which is forbidden. A small amount is clearly for the meal at hand. This matches רבי יוסי's objection, which spoke about large and small amounts.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
This is what he means:
One may not make a large amount of salt water,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה הוּא מֵי מֶלַח מוּעָטִין.
phrases.english: but one may make a small amount of salt water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is quantity: large is forbidden, small is permitted.

steps.title: Did רבי יוסי mean to forbid or to permit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי again and asks: by saying both amounts are the same, does he forbid both or permit both?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: But isn't it brine, whether a lot or a little? They asked: Is רבי יוסי forbidding or permitting?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי יוסי's words because they can be read two ways. It asks which way he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'large and small are the same' could lead in two directions. Both could be forbidden because even a little is brine, or both could be permitted because even a lot is just salt water. The משנה never states his conclusion outright.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבי יוסי must be stricter just because he argues. His point that the amounts are equal could support permitting both just as well as forbidding both.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא הוּא הֵילְמֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: But isn't it brine,
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the משנה's words in order to analyze them.

phrases.english: whether a lot or a little?
They asked:
Did Rabbi Yosei mean to forbid or to permit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֶאֱסוֹר אוֹ לְהַתִּיר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוסי make both amounts forbidden or both permitted?

steps.title: רב יהודה: רבי יוסי permits
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says רבי יוסי permits, because the משנה does not use the phrase 'רבי יוסי forbids'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: To permit, since the משנה does not say 'רבי יוסי forbids.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives his answer: רבי יוסי permits both amounts. His proof comes from what the משנה leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי meant to forbid everything, the משנה would normally say so plainly with 'רבי יוסי אוסר'. Since it does not, רב יהודה concludes that רבי יוסי permits.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it does not teach (proof from what is missing)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: To permit.
Since it does not teach 'Rabbi Yosei forbids.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי permits, as shown by the absence of the word 'אוסר'.

steps.title: רבה: the end of the משנה shows he forbids
steps.stepSummary: רבה pushes back: the משנה ends with 'this is the permitted salt water', which implies the ordinary kind is forbidden according to רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: Since the end of the משנה teaches 'and this is the salt water that is permitted,' it follows that רבי יוסי means to forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה challenges רב יהודה with the last line of the משנה (step 3).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי allowed all salt water, he would have no reason to describe a special permitted method using oil. Offering a permitted way only makes sense if the normal way is forbidden. That evidence is stronger than the missing word 'אוסר'.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (a response or challenge)
The end part of the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbah said to him:
Since the end clause teaches
'and this is the salt water that is permitted,'
it follows that Rabbi Yosei means to forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה: הָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that רבי יוסי permits
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A special 'permitted' method implies that ordinary salt water is forbidden in רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: רבה and רבי יוחנן: רבי יוסי forbids
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that רבי יוסי forbids, and רבי יוחנן says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: To forbid. And רבי יוחנן also said: To forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is settled: רבי יוסי forbids salt water in any amount, unless it is made the oil way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלא ('rather') sets aside רב יהודה's view. רבי יוחנן's agreement adds a second major voice for the strict reading.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, both large and small amounts of plain salt water are forbidden on שבת. Only the oil method is allowed.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbah said: To forbid.
And Rabbi Yochanan likewise said: To forbid.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי forbids all ordinary salt water.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the reading: the first view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought as support. It first repeats the first view: a large amount for pickling is forbidden, and a small amount for eating is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught so: One may not make a large amount of salt water to put on pickles in a גיסטרא, but one may make a small amount and eat his bread with it and put it into a cooked dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins bringing a ברייתא to back up the conclusion. This part gives the first view and sets up רבי יוסי's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds a detail the משנה left out. The large amount is forbidden because it is meant for pickling vegetables in a גיסטרא. This fits שמואל's explanation in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)
A flat earthenware shard or vessel used for pickling

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
One may not make a large amount of salt water
to put on the pickles that are in a pickling vessel.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה הוּא מֵי מֶלַח מוּעָטִין,
phrases.english: But one may make a small amount of salt water,
and eat his bread with it,
and put it into the cooked dish.

steps.raayaObject: The conclusion of רבה and רבי יוחנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that records the same dispute in fuller form

steps.title: רבי יוסי explicitly forbids both amounts
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי says plainly that both large and small amounts are forbidden. Otherwise people would think a small מלאכה is allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: Because one is large and one is small, one is forbidden and one permitted? People will say a large labor is forbidden and a small labor is permitted! Rather, both are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual proof. In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי clearly says 'both are forbidden', just as רבה and רבי יוחנן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי is worried about a wrong lesson. If size decided the matter, people would conclude that a small amount of מלאכה is fine on שבת. So he forbids both amounts, which settles the question from step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it just because...? (a rhetorical rejection)
People will say (concern about a mistaken conclusion)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוסי's concern is a matter of principle: the amount can never decide whether something counts as מלאכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַלָּלוּ מְרוּבִּין וְהַלָּלוּ מוּעָטִין
phrases.english: Is it because these are many and those are few
that these are forbidden and those are permitted?
People will say: a large labor is forbidden,
but a small labor is permitted!
Rather, both are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַלָּלוּ מְרוּבִּין
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's explicit words in the ברייתא: 'אלו ואלו אסורין הן'

steps.title: The permitted salt water according to the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying one may combine oil with salt or oil with water, as long as water and salt are not put together first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the permitted salt water: one puts oil and salt, or oil and water, as long as one does not put water and salt together at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא wraps up by explaining the allowed method in more detail, matching the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What is forbidden is mixing water and salt directly at the start, because that is how brine is made. If oil goes in first with either the salt or the water, the mixture is made differently and is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Water and salt (the normal brine mix)

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion is that רבי יוסי forbids all plain salt water. It is permitted only when oil is mixed in first with the salt or the water, never water and salt alone at the start.

phrases.english: And this is the salt water that is permitted:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן שֶׁמֶן וּמֶלַח אוֹ שֶׁמֶן וּמַיִם,
phrases.english: one puts oil and salt, or oil and water,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתֵּן מַיִם וּמֶלַח לְכַתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.english: as long as he does not put water and salt together at the start.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Salt water is permitted only if oil is mixed in first. Water and salt may not be combined directly at the start.

steps.title: A memory aid for the next three teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן of three words: עזין, צנון, אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Strong, radish, and citron' is a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next section. It gives three key words so we can remember three teachings of רבי יהודה בר חביבא that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one teaching. עזין stands for strong salt water, צנון for salting a radish, and אתרוג for the teaching about foods that are hard to digest.

phrases.english: Strong, radish, and citron are a mnemonic.
phrases.notes: Each word hints at one upcoming teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the salt-water discussion to a new set of related teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mnemonic for three teachings of רבי יהודה בר חביבא.

steps.title: One may not make strong salt water on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר חביבא teaches that one may not make מי מלח עזין on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר חביבא taught: One may not prepare strong salt water.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first teaching from the memory aid. Making very strong salt water on שבת is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the earlier discussion. Even according to the view that permits ordinary salt water, very strong salt water is different, because it is used for pickling and preserving.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who taught these three teachings

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Ḥaviva taught:
One may not prepare strong salt water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First teaching hinted at by the mnemonic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Strong salt water may not be prepared on שבת.

steps.title: What counts as strong salt water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of מי מלח עזין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is strong salt water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how strong the salt water has to be before it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some salt water is allowed, so we need a clear line. The question asks for a test that shows when salt water becomes 'strong'.

phrases.english: What is strong salt water?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Water that an egg floats in
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף בר אבא say it is salt water strong enough for an egg to float.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף בר אבא both said: any water in which an egg floats.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give a simple test: if an egg floats in it, it is strong salt water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg sinks in plain water. It floats only when a lot of salt is dissolved, so the floating egg is a practical way to tell the water is very salty.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef bar Abba
who both said:
Any water in which an egg floats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of definition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Strong salt water is water in which an egg floats.

steps.title: How much salt is that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the actual amount of salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the ratio of salt to water that makes strong salt water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The egg test describes the result. This question asks for a measured amount.

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: A one-word question asking for the measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a numerical measure for the definition just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The ratio of salt to water.

steps.title: Two-thirds salt, one-third water
steps.stepSummary: אביי says strong salt water is two parts salt to one part water.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: two-thirds salt and one-third water.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the amount: two-thirds salt and one-third water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is far saltier than ordinary salt water for dipping. It shows that strong salt water is a preserving liquid, not just seasoning.

phrases.english: Abaye said: two-thirds salt
and one-third water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'how much' question.

steps.title: What is strong salt water used for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this very salty water is made for.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose is it made?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why anyone would make such salty water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing its use helps explain why it is forbidden. It is made for a food-processing purpose, not for simple dipping.

phrases.english: For what purpose do they make it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the use of the salt water just defined.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of strong salt water.

steps.title: It is made for fish brine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says strong salt water is made for מורייס, a fish brine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: for מורייס (fish brine).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers that it is used to make מורייס, a salty fish sauce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making מורייס is a preserving and processing job. This shows why strong salt water is treated more strictly than plain salt water for dipping.

keyTerms.meaning: מורייס, a brine made from fish

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: for fish brine (muraisa).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of purpose and closes the first teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is made for fish brine (מורייס).
steps.whatToRemember: מי מלח עזין means water an egg floats in, about two-thirds salt, made for fish brine. It is forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: One may not salt a radish or an egg on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר חביבא's second teaching: no salting a radish or an egg on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר חביבא taught: One may not salt a radish or an egg on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second teaching from the memory aid. It forbids salting a radish or an egg on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salting can change and improve a food, much like pickling it. This ברייתא treats that as a forbidden kind of food processing on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Ḥaviva taught:
One may not salt a radish or an egg on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second teaching hinted at by the mnemonic (צנון).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salting a radish or an egg on שבת is forbidden.

steps.title: Radish forbidden, egg permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב חזקיה in the name of אביי splits the cases: a radish is forbidden, an egg is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חזקיה said in the name of אביי: a radish is forbidden, and an egg is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a different ruling. He agrees about the radish but permits salting an egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא put the radish and the egg together. Here they are separated: salting a radish counts as processing it, while salting an egg does not.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥizkiya said in the name of Abaye:
A radish is forbidden, and an egg is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with part of the ברייתא by permitting the egg.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salting a radish is forbidden; salting an egg is permitted.

steps.title: רב נחמן used to salt radishes, thinking it ruined them
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says he once salted radishes on שבת, because שמואל taught that sharpness is good for a radish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: At first I used to salt radishes. I said: I am ruining it, since שמואל said that sharpness is good for a radish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן tells how he used to act: he salted radishes on שבת. He thought salting made them worse, not better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning came from שמואל: a radish is best when sharp. Salt reduces the sharpness, so salting seemed to harm the radish. Harming a food is not forbidden processing.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
At first I used to salt radishes,
for I said: I am ruining it,
since Shmuel said:
For a radish, its sharpness is good.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה מָלַחְנָא פּוּגְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב נחמן's earlier reasoning about salting a radish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, salting a radish was thought to ruin it and so was allowed.

steps.title: רב נחמן stops salting, but still dips
steps.stepSummary: After hearing from עולא that in ארץ ישראל people salt large piles of radishes, רב נחמן stopped salting them on שבת but still dips them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once I heard this, that when עולא came he said that in the West they salt pile after pile, I do not salt anymore, but I certainly dip.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן changed his practice. He no longer salts radishes on שבת, but he still dips each piece in salt as he eats it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא reported that in ארץ ישראל people salt whole piles of radishes, so salting is a normal way to improve them. That makes it processing and forbidden. Dipping a bite while eating is just eating, not preparing the food.
steps.confusionAlert: Salting and dipping are not the same. Salting the radish ahead of time counts as processing it and is forbidden. Dipping each bite in salt while eating is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Salting a radish on שבת is forbidden because it improves it, but dipping it in salt while eating is fine.

phrases.english: Once I heard this,
that when Ulla came he said
in the West they salt pile after pile,
I no longer salt,
but I certainly dip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses רב נחמן's earlier practice based on new information.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Salting radishes on שבת is forbidden as an improvement, but dipping them in salt is permitted.

steps.title: Citron, radish and egg are hard to digest
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר חביבא's third teaching: without their outer layer, an אתרוג, a radish and an egg would never leave the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר חביבא taught: an אתרוג, a radish and an egg, if not for their outer peel, would never leave the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third teaching from the memory aid, a health teaching about digestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These foods are very hard to digest. Their outer layer helps them pass through the body. It is grouped here because the same תנא taught it and it mentions radishes and eggs.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Ḥaviva taught:
A citron, a radish, and an egg,
if not for their outer peel,
they would never come out of the intestines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third teaching hinted at by the mnemonic (אתרוג).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A citron, a radish and an egg are very hard to digest, and their outer layer helps them pass.

steps.title: No one ever drowned in the Sea of Sodom
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports from ארץ ישראל that no person has ever drowned in the Sea of Sodom.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: No man has ever drowned in the Sea of Sodom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brings a new fact from ארץ ישראל: the Sea of Sodom is so salty that a person cannot sink in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the salt theme of the last few steps. The extra salt makes the water heavy, so people float. Later this fact will matter for the laws of healing on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: When [a sage] came from ארץ ישראל to בבל
The Sea of Sodom (the Dead Sea)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Never has a man drowned
in the Sea of Sodom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of salt-related teachings with a new statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No person ever drowns in the Sea of Sodom.

steps.title: רב יוסף says the wording is backwards
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects that saying 'a man does not drown' implies that a plank of wood does sink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Sodom is overturned, and his words are overturned! Is it a man who does not drown, while a plank sinks?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the wording of רב דימי's statement. Mentioning only a man sounds as if other things, like wood, would sink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood floats even in ordinary water, so the fact that a man does not sink is the bigger news. Singling out the man seems to imply that wood does sink, which is absurd. רב יוסף makes a joke out of it: Sodom was 'overturned', and so are these words.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Sodom is overturned, and his words are overturned.
Is it a man who does not drown,
but a plank sinks?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the phrasing of רב דימי's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רב דימי's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying only a man does not drown implies that a plank does sink, which is obviously false.

steps.title: אביי explains: 'not only a plank, but even a man'
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רב דימי was speaking in a 'it goes without saying' style. A plank floats everywhere, and even a man floats in the Sea of Sodom.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: He was speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that a plank does not sink, since it doesn't sink in any water in the world. But even a man, who drowns in all the other waters of the world, does not drown in the Sea of Sodom.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the wording. רב דימי mentioned the man because that is the surprising part, and the plank is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a לא מיבעיא, the speaker states the surprising case and the obvious case is included automatically. A plank floats in every body of water, so it floats here too. The new information is that even a person floats in this sea.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary [to say]: a style where the surprising case is stated and the obvious one is included

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
He is speaking in a 'no need to say' style:
There is no need to say a plank

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּכׇל מֵימוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם לָא טָבַע,
phrases.english: which even in all the waters of the world does not sink,
but even a man
who drowns in all the waters of the world,
in the Sea of Sodom does not drown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement singles out a man, which implies that a plank sinks.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plank is too obvious to mention. The חידוש is that even a man floats.

steps.title: What practical law comes from this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference this fact makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need to know this fact. It is setting up the next step, which will show a halachic use for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A geography fact needs a reason to be in a halachic discussion. The answer will connect it to bathing on שבת.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the halachic relevance of the fact established in Steps 26-28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The halachic consequence of the Sea of Sodom's unusual water.

steps.title: Washing in Sea of Sodom water on שבת is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבין, walking with רבי ירמיה by the Dead Sea, asked whether one may wash in its water on שבת. רבי ירמיה permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in this case: רבין was walking behind רבי ירמיה on the shore of the Sea of Sodom. He asked him: May one wash with this water on שבת? He answered: It is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a story. This water has healing power, and the question was whether bathing in it counts as forbidden healing on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that even a person floats shows how extremely salty this water is. That raises the question of whether bathing in it counts as forbidden healing on שבת. רבי ירמיה rules that ordinary washing in it is allowed, since it is not obviously medical treatment.

phrases.english: Like this case, where Ravin

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל אֲחוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
phrases.english: was walking behind Rabbi Yirmeya
on the shore of the Sea of Sodom.
He said to him: What is the law about washing
with this water on Shabbat?
He said to him: It is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרָבִין הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'practical difference' question with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fact relates to washing in Dead Sea water on שבת, which is permitted.

steps.title: May one close and open the eyes in that water?
steps.stepSummary: רבין asks a follow-up: while washing, may one blink so that the water enters the eyes?
steps.simpleTranslation: What about closing and opening [the eyes]?
steps.whatsHappening: רבין asks a harder question. Letting the water get into the eyes by blinking looks more like medical treatment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simple bathing was permitted. Deliberately working the healing water into the eyes looks like real treatment, so the case is harder. This sets up רבי ירמיה's answer.

phrases.english: What about closing and opening [the eyes]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question to the permission to wash.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether blinking so the healing water enters the eyes is forbidden healing on שבת.

steps.title: A similar case: wine and saliva on the eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה hasn't heard this exact case, but he quotes a similar teaching from אבוה דשמואל and לוי. Wine inside the eye is forbidden and on the eyelid is permitted. Bland saliva is forbidden even on the eyelid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: This I did not hear, but something similar I heard. רבי זירא said it, sometimes in the name of רב מתנה and sometimes in the name of מר עוקבא. Both said it in the name of שמואל's father and לוי. One said: wine inside the eye is forbidden; on the eye it is permitted. The other said: bland saliva is forbidden even on the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers by comparing the question to a known ruling about putting things on the eye on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting something inside the eye is real treatment, so it is forbidden. Putting it on the outside of the eye is not obvious treatment, so it is permitted. Bland saliva (from someone who has not eaten yet) is a well-known remedy, so it is forbidden even outside. By comparison, blinking to let the water inside would be like wine inside the eye, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: On top of the eye (outside, on the eyelid)
Bland saliva, from someone who has not eaten since waking

steps.confusionAlert: Two rulings are given, but the text says only 'one said... and one said'. It does not tell us which of the two sages said which. The next steps try to figure that out.

phrases.english: He said to him: This I did not hear,
something similar to it I heard.
For Rabbi Zeira said,

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב מַתְנָה
phrases.english: sometimes he said it in the name of Rav Mattana

phrases.aramaic: וְזִימְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּמָר עוּקְבָא,
phrases.english: and sometimes he said it in the name of Mar Ukva,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַרְוַויְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל וְלֵוִי אָמְרִין,
phrases.english: and both of them said it in the name of Shmuel's father and Levi:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: יַיִן, בְּתוֹךְ הָעַיִן — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: One said: Wine inside the eye is forbidden,
on the eye it is permitted.
And one said: Bland saliva,
even on the eye, is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי, כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהּ שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבין's question by comparison to a known teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Inside the eye is forbidden and on the eye is permitted, so blinking the water in is forbidden. Bland saliva is forbidden even on the eye.

steps.title: Proof that שמואל's father said the wine ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove that שמואל's father said the wine ruling. שמואל himself permits soaking bread in wine and putting it on the eye, and he presumably learned that from his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that שמואל's father is the one who said wine inside the eye is forbidden and on the eye is permitted. For שמואל said: A person may soak his bread in wine and put it on the eye on שבת. From whom did he hear this? Wasn't it from his father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to identify which sage said the wine ruling, using a matching statement of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's ruling matches the 'on the eye is permitted' part of the wine teaching. The assumption is that a son learns from his father. So the wine ruling would belong to אבוה דשמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: From whom did he hear it?

phrases.english: Conclude that Shmuel's father is the one who said
wine inside the eye is forbidden,
on the eye it is permitted,
since Shmuel said:
A person may soak his bread in wine
and put it on the eye on Shabbat.
From whom did he hear it?
Didn't he hear it from his father?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to assign the unattributed rulings of Step 32.
steps.raayaObject: That אבוה דשמואל said the wine ruling
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's own ruling permitting wine-soaked bread on the eye, presumably learned from his father

steps.title: The proof fails: we can't tell who said which
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. שמואל also said the saliva ruling, so by the same logic his father would have said both, leaving לוי with nothing. Rather, שמואל learned one from each, and we don't know which.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to your logic, take שמואל's statement that bland saliva is forbidden even on the eye: from whom did he hear it? If from his father, then did לוי not say even one ruling?! Rather, he heard one from his father and one from לוי, and we don't know which came from whom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the proof does not work, because שמואל taught both rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'שמואל taught it, so his father said it' were valid, it would apply to both rulings. Then לוי would have said nothing, which contradicts the report that each sage said one. So שמואל learned from both sages, and his own statements can't tell us who said which.
steps.whatToRemember: Wine inside the eye on שבת is forbidden and on the eye is permitted. Bland saliva is forbidden even on the eye. The rulings come from אבוה דשמואל and לוי, but we can't tell which sage said which.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
that which Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹק תָּפֵל אֲפִילּוּ עַל גַּבֵּי הָעַיִן אָסוּר,
phrases.english: bland saliva even on the eye is forbidden,
from whom did he hear it?
If you say he heard it from his father,
then Levi did not say even one?!
Rather: one he heard from his father
and one he heard from Levi,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדְעִינַן הֵי מֵאֲבוּהּ הֵי מִלֵּוִי.
phrases.english: and we do not know which was from his father and which from Levi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 33.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attempt to attribute the wine ruling to אבוה דשמואל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same logic would give both rulings to שמואל's father and leave לוי with none.

steps.title: Eye salve soaked before שבת may be put on the eyes
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא quotes שמואל: one may soak eye salves before שבת and put them on the eyes on שבת without worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא said in the name of שמואל: A person may soak eye salves on ערב שבת and put them on his eyes on שבת, and he need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling about eye treatment on שבת: salve that was prepared beforehand may go on the outside of the eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking the salve on שבת itself would be preparing medicine, so it is done beforehand. Putting it on the eyelid matches the 'on the eye is permitted' principle from the wine ruling.

phrases.english: Mar Ukva said in the name of Shmuel:
A person may soak eye salves on Shabbat eve
and put them on his eyes on Shabbat,
and he need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related ruling on eye treatment on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salve soaked before שבת may be placed on the eyes on שבת.

steps.title: בר לואי: שמואל didn't permit blinking it in
steps.stepSummary: בר לואי saw מר עוקבא opening and closing his eyes with the salve on, and objected that שמואל never allowed that much.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר לואי was standing before מר עוקבא. He saw him closing and opening [his eyes]. He said to him: All this, Master שמואל certainly did not permit.
steps.whatsHappening: In this story, someone challenges מר עוקבא's behavior as going beyond שמואל's permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allowed salve on top of the eyes. Blinking works it inside the eye, which is like 'wine inside the eye' and forbidden. This matches the earlier answer to רבין's question.

phrases.aramaic: בַּר לֵוַאי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר עוּקְבָא.
phrases.english: Bar Liva'ei was standing before Mar Ukva.
He saw him closing and opening his eyes.
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי הַאי וַדַּאי לָא שְׁרָא מָר שְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: All this, Master Shmuel certainly did not permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּי הַאי וַדַּאי לָא שְׁרָא מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits שמואל's permission through a story.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר עוקבא's practice of blinking with the salve
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל permitted salve only on the eye. Working it inside by blinking is beyond that permission.

steps.title: Better than any salve: cold water and warm washing
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי asked מר עוקבא for שמואל's salves. מר עוקבא agreed to send them but passed on שמואל's advice: cold water in the morning and warm washing of hands and feet at night beat all salves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי sent to מר עוקבא: Please send us some of Master שמואל's salves. He replied: I will send them, so you won't say I am stingy. But this is what שמואל said: A drop of cold water in the morning and washing hands and feet in hot water in the evening are better than all the salves in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: Another story about the salves, ending with a piece of health advice from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר עוקבא sends the salves so he won't look stingy. He adds that simple daily habits protect the eyes better than any medicine.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי יַנַּאי לְמָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai sent to Mar Ukva:
Let the master send us
some of those eye salves of Master Shmuel.
He sent him: I will certainly send them to you,
so that you do not say I am stingy,
but this is what Shmuel said:
Better a drop of cold water in the morning
and washing hands and feet in hot water in the evening
than all the eye salves in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי יַנַּאי לְמָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of שמואל's eye salves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cold water in the morning and warm washing of hands and feet at night are better than all eye salves.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same health advice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה gives the same advice, supporting שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught so: רבי מונא said in the name of רבי יהודה: A drop of cold water in the morning and washing hands and feet in the evening are better than all the salves in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as שמואל, as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier source confirms שמואל's advice almost word for word. The only difference is that the ברייתא does not mention hot water for the evening washing.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports it)

steps.whatToRemember: Eye salve soaked before שבת may go on top of the eyes, but not worked inside by blinking. Simple cold and warm washing is the best eye care.

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מוּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Mona said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda:
Better a drop of cold water in the morning
and washing hands and feet in the evening
than all the eye salves in the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's advice with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's health advice about cold and warm washing
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי מונא in the name of רבי יהודה

steps.title: A hand that touches sensitive body parts should be cut off
steps.stepSummary: The same sage who gave the health advice in the previous ברייתא used to say that a hand which touches the eye, nose, mouth, ear, a wound, the אמה, or the פי טבעת 'should be cut off.' This is a strong way of warning that touching these places harms them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He used to say: A hand to the eye should be cut off. A hand to the nose should be cut off. A hand to the mouth should be cut off. A hand to the ear should be cut off. A hand to a wound should be cut off. A hand to the private part should be cut off. A hand to the anus should be cut off. A hand... (the list continues on the next amud)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with health advice from the same sage and quotes his list of body parts a hand should not touch. The list is not finished yet, because the last word 'יָד' begins the next item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new legal argument. It adds more practical health advice, following the topic of eye salves and washing. The phrase 'should be cut off' is a sharp way of saying that touching these places is harmful. רש"י explains that it means touching them in the morning before washing the hands. For the אמה, the concern is also about arousing oneself.

keyTerms.meaning: He used to say. This brings in more teachings from the same sage.
Should be cut off. A strong expression of warning, not a real punishment.
A wound, such as the cut left from bloodletting
The anus (literally 'the mouth of the ring')

steps.confusionAlert: 'תִּיקָּצֵץ' does not mean anyone actually cuts off a hand. It is a vivid way of saying 'this is very harmful, don't do it.'

phrases.english: He used to say:
phrases.notes: Refers to the sage of the previous ברייתא, who gave health advice in the name of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: A hand to the eye should be cut off.
phrases.notes: Touching the eye harms it. רש"י: before washing the hands in the morning.

phrases.english: A hand to the nose should be cut off.
A hand to the mouth should be cut off.
A hand to the ear should be cut off.
A hand to a wound should be cut off.
phrases.notes: Such as the cut left from bloodletting

phrases.english: A hand to the private part should be cut off.
phrases.notes: So that he does not arouse himself

phrases.english: A hand to the anus should be cut off.
phrases.notes: So that he does not make himself ill

phrases.english: A hand...
phrases.notes: This word starts the next item in the list, which continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with more health teachings from the same sage whose advice about cold and warm water was quoted in Step 38.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should not touch the eye, nose, mouth, ear, a wound, the אמה, or the פי טבעת with his hand, because it is harmful. The strong wording 'should be cut off' shows how serious the warning is.
